exposure.needed: which package images the environment references are hosted in private (authenticated) repositories, since repository privacy is registry-side state not carried in any manifest, values key or flag named by the evidence

original.statement: Crossplane 2.0.0 enables extracting package.yaml from private repositories.

exposure.needed: whether operators run the `crossplane xpkg extract` CLI command (cmd/crank) against package images in private, authenticated registries; this is CLI usage on operator machines, not in-cluster configuration

corrected.statement: Crossplane 2.0.0's `crossplane xpkg extract` CLI command now uses default registry auth, so it can extract package.yaml from private repositories. Only operators who run this CLI command against private registries are affected; the Crossplane installation in the cluster is not.

decision.reason: The linked PR [ev-fce5b51d8226] says the change adds default auth to the `crossplane xpkg extract` CLI command when it fetches from a remote registry, and [ev-550788c9f271] shows that cmd/crank/xpkg/extract.go is the only file changed. So the change is to the CLI, not to how Crossplane in the cluster handles the package images an environment references. The proposed exposure, which keys on in-cluster package images hosted in private repositories, flags the wrong environments. Exposure really depends on whether operators run `crossplane xpkg extract` against a private registry. That is CLI usage, which no manifest, values key or flag records.
